question.problem:
A rinse tank initially holds $240\,\text{L}$ of water containing $9\,\text{kg}$ of dissolved dye.
A solution containing $0.025\,\text{kg/L}$ of dissolved dye is pumped into the tank at a rate of $16\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed water is drained out at a rate of $24\,\text{L/min}.$ If the amount of dye $Q(t),$ in kilograms, in the tank $t$ minutes after pumping begins is given by

$$
Q(t)=\alpha \,(1-\frac{t}{30})+\beta {(1-\frac{t}{30})}^{3}
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants, what is the value of $\alpha -\beta ?$
question.worked_solution:
Since $Q$ is the amount of dye in the tank at time $t,$ the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t,$ in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which dye enters the tank minus the rate at which dye leaves the tank.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{kg}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which dye enters the tank.

First, note that a water solution containing $0.025\,\text{kg/L}$ of dye enters the tank at a rate of $16\,\text{L/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *dye* enters the tank is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(0.025\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot (16\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(0.025\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}})\cdot (16\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =0.4\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which dye exits the tank.

To find the rate at which dye leaves the tank, we must first determine the volume of water in the tank at time $t.$

The tank initially contains $240\,\text{L}$ of water; a solution enters at $16\,\text{L/min}$ and leaves at $24\,\text{L/min}.$
As a result, the amount of water in the tank after $t$ minutes is 

$$
240+16t-24t=(240-8t)\,\text{L}.
$$

Since $Q$ is the amount of dye in the tank, the *concentration* of the mixed solution at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{240-8t}\,\text{kg/L}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed water leaves at a rate of $24\,\text{L/min},$ *dye* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(24\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{240-8t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}}) \\  & =(24\,\frac{\cancel{\text{L}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{240-8t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\cancel{\text{L}}}) \\  & =\frac{24Q}{240-8t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{3Q}{30-t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

The rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit. Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =0.4-\frac{3Q}{30-t}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{30-t}Q=0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.

This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(t) & ={e}^{\int 3/(30-t)\,dt} \\  & ={e}^{-3\operatorname{ln}⁡|30-t|} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(30-t)^{-3}} \\  & =(30-t)^{-3}\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the differential equation by $I(t)=(30-t)^{-3}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}(30-t)^{-3}\cdot (\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{3}{30-t}Q) & =(30-t)^{-3}\cdot 0.4 \\ (30-t)^{-3}\frac{dQ}{dt}+3(30-t)^{-4}Q & =0.4(30-t)^{-3} \\ \frac{d}{dt}(Q(30-t)^{-3}) & =0.4(30-t)^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{d}{dt}(Q(30-t)^{-3})\,dt & =\int 0.4(30-t)^{-3}\,dt \\ Q(30-t)^{-3} & =0.4\cdot \frac{1}{2}(30-t)^{-2}+C \\ Q(t) & =0.2(30-t)+C(30-t)^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $C$ is a constant of integration.

We're told that the tank initially contains $9\,\text{kg}$ of dye. So, we can apply the initial condition $Q(0)=9,$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(0) & =9 \\ C(30-0)^{3}+0.2(30-0) & =9 \\ C(30)^{3}+6 & =9 \\ C & =\frac{3}{{30}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(t) & =0.2(30-t)+\frac{3}{{30}^{3}}(30-t)^{3} \\  & =0.2\cdot 30\,(\frac{30-t}{30})+3{(\frac{30-t}{30})}^{3} \\  & =6\,(1-\frac{t}{30})+3{(1-\frac{t}{30})}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have $\alpha =6,\beta =3,$ and

$$
\alpha -\beta =6-3=3.
$$
